gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 65 W is a fixed row in each charger's own port table and not a property of a 100 W rating: techtest.org (Michael Barton, 23 Nov 2026) lists the 100 W Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 at 45 W + 45 W with two USB-C ports in use, so it misses the 65 W line.
standout_why: Compared against cadiens.com (both pages), racksandwatts.com, computingforgeeks.com, thisusb.com/guides/best-usb-c-chargers, specseveryday.com, techfromalex.com and Anker's cited service page. Between them they already carry the Anker 65+35 and UGREEN 65+30 tables, the 'laptop on C1' rule, the 5 A cable rule ('A 3A cable caps you at 60W', computingforgeeks), a UGREEN charging pause on plug/unplug (cadiens) and 'the charger renegotiates' (thisusb). None names a 100 W charger that fails the line: no page gives the AH22's two-port split, and ChatGPT's second answer only says generically that 'some chargers split 60 W + 40 W or 45 W + 45 W'. None quotes Anker's own wording that a plug or unplug makes the charger re-evaluate distribution with a brief interruption, and none gives techtest.org's PPS ceiling (5-11 V) for the A2688.
decides: It confirms the Anker Prime A2688 and UGREEN Nexode 100W picks and removes one of our linked rows. The Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 (100 W, 3× USB-C, $59.99) gives the laptop 45 W once a phone is plugged in (techtest.org), so it must be named as left out; the page's breakpoint sentence 'a 100 W charger keeps 65 W' needs the qualifier 'if its two-port table says so'. For the Anker, the 65 W exists only on the top port: Anker's table gives USB-C2 + USB-A 12 W + 12 W, and Anker's product page says to use the upper port for laptops. Anker's US store today shows the A2688 at $45.99 as a pre-order shipping Nov 25 - Dec 5, 2026, which the price row must state. techtest.org measured PPS on the A2688 only to 11 V, which matters for ranking on phone mode (a Samsung on C2). I could not open UGREEN's own pages, so the UGREEN 65+30 figure still rests on rival pages and our record, not on a maker page I read.

findings.label: Watts per port with two USB-C ports in use
findings.value: 45 W + 45 W (USB-C 1 + 2); 45 W + 45 W + 10 W with all three
findings.source_title: Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 im Test: 100W USB-C-Ladegerät mit Display und AVS (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 23 Nov 2026)
findings.note: Reviewer's port table: 'USB-C 1 + 2 = 45 W + 45 W'; 'Entsprechend werden die Ports gedrosselt, je nachdem, wie viele du nutzt.' Each port alone gives 100 W (5V/3A, 9V/3A, 12V/3A, 15V/3A, 20V/5A). The article does not say whether the split is fixed or adapts to draw. 45 W is below the 65 W line.

findings.label: PPS / AVS range (single port)
findings.value: PPS 5-20 V at up to 5 A on all USB-C ports; AVS 9-20 V / 5 A
findings.source_title: Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 im Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton)
findings.note: AVS is listed without naming a port. Ranges in two-port mode are not given.

findings.label: Maker's port table
findings.value: One port 100 W; USB-C1 + USB-C2 65 W + 35 W; USB-C1 + USB-A 65 W + 22.5 W; USB-C2 + USB-A 12 W + 12 W (24 W max); three ports 89 W max
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (100W, 3 Ports, Prime) - Anker product information (A2688)
findings.note: The 65 W belongs to USB-C1. A laptop on USB-C2 gets 35 W with a phone on C1, and 12 W with a phone on USB-A. This page is one ChatGPT cited.

findings.label: Maker's instruction on port and cable
findings.value: "When using both USB-C ports simultaneously, use the upper port for charging laptops." "For optimal 100W charging, use an E-Marker cable." "Charging cables for compatible devices are not included and must be purchased separately."
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (100W, 3 Ports, GaN) - Anker US
findings.note: Per-port spec on the page: USB-C1/C2 5V⎓3A, 9V⎓3A, 15V⎓3A, 20V⎓5A (100W Max). The page lists two ports as '100W Max' and three as '89W Max' without the per-port split; the split is on the service page.

findings.label: Price and availability on Anker's US store
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (100W, 3 Ports, GaN) - Anker US
findings.note: Read from the product page; storecheck.py returned HTTP 404 for this URL, so the variant was not confirmed by the tool. No sale end date is stated. ChatGPT showed $69.99 at B&H. Amazon was not read.

findings.label: Voltage steps and PPS range measured by a named reviewer
findings.value: USB-C: 5V/3A, 9V/3A, 15V/3A, 20V/5A, no 12 V step; PPS 5-11 V at up to 5 A
findings.source_title: Ist das Anker Prime 100W das beste kompakte Ladegerät? Detaillierter Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 7 Nov 2024)
findings.note: Single-port figures for the A2688; the article does not cover what each port offers in two-port mode. PPS stops at 11 V, short of the 20 V PPS the page rules cite for a Galaxy S26 Ultra's top tier.

findings.label: Sustained 100 W and efficiency
findings.value: Holds 100 W for about one hour before overheating and throttling; efficiency 86.6 % to 91.1 %
findings.source_title: Ist das Anker Prime 100W das beste kompakte Ladegerät? Detaillierter Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton)
findings.note: "Es schafft die 100 W für ca. eine Stunde, bevor es überhitzt und die Leistung drosselt." Measured at full 100 W single-port load, not at the 65 + 35 W split.

findings.label: Why the laptop's watts change the moment a phone is plugged in (Anker's words, a sibling 100 W model)
findings.value: "When a device is connected or disconnected, the charger re-evaluates power distribution." "This may cause a brief interruption in charging, which is normal." "If compatible, the charger will automatically switch to 95W + 5W mode after about 1 minute."
findings.source_title: Anker Charger (100W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) FAQ - Anker support
findings.note: This is the Smart Display model, not the A2688; the page gives no model number or date. The interruption sentence is Anker's answer about switching between two-port and three-port use. Its Q5 mentions the split changing from 95 + 5 W to 70 + 30 W after a plug or unplug on USB-C1. It shows the allocation is set by plug events and firmware.

findings.label: Why 65 W needs a 5 A cable
findings.value: 65 W at 20 V is 3.25 A; USB-IF: "USB PD was limited to 100W using a solution based on 20V using USB Type-C cables rated at 5A."
findings.note: Arithmetic: 65 ÷ 20 = 3.25 A. The USB-IF page does not state the 3 A limit for unmarked cables. A rival already states the consequence: computingforgeeks.com/best-gan-charger-laptop/ says 'A 3A cable caps you at 60W (20V at 3A) whatever the charger can do.'
